findings.location: ** What A Revival Of Religion Is – Charles Grandison Finney – The Belknap Press Of Harvard University
findings.source_quote: “A revival is not a miracle, or dependent on a miracle, in any sense. It is a purely philosophical result of the right use of the constituted means”.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the translated phrase «Une réveil n'est pas un miracle…» with the grammatically correct «Un réveil n'est pas un miracle…». Maintain the rest of the sentence as translated.
findings.translation_quote: «Une réveil n'est pas un miracle, ni dépendant d'un miracle, en aucun sens. C'est un résultat purement philosophique de la bonne utilisation des moyens constitués».

findings.source_quote: The contemporary emergence of thousands of “hit and run” ministries should cause us concern.
findings.suggested_fix: The translation renders “hit and run” ministries as «ministères “coup d'éclair”», which is awkward and non‑idiomatic in French. Replace «ministères “coup d'éclair”» with a more natural equivalent such as «ministères éphémères» or «ministères “coup d'éclair” (ministères éphémères)» depending on desired literalness. Keep the HTML structure unchanged.
findings.translation_quote: «L'émergence contemporaine de milliers de ministères « coup d'éclair » devrait nous préoccuper.»

findings.location: If anyone was capable of articulating a flourish of orations in an accurate philosophical language it would have been the Apostle Paul.
findings.source_quote: If anyone was capable of articulating a flourish of orations in an accurate philosophical language it would have been the Apostle Paul.
findings.suggested_fix: The translator rendered “a flourish of orations” as «un éclat d'oraisons», which is odd in French. Replace «un éclat d'oraisons» with a more idiomatic phrasing such as «un épanchement d'oraisons», «des oraisons brillantes» or «un tour d'éloquence» to better convey the English meaning. Preserve surrounding tags and punctuation.
findings.translation_quote: «Si quelqu'un était capable d'articuler un éclat d'oraisons dans un langage philosophique précis, ce fut l'apôtre Paul.»
